evidence: compare.py:91-93 calls sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read=resolved) and parsed.sql(dialect=resolved, normalize=True, pretty=False). pyproject.toml:44 pins sqlglot>=25.0,<31. In that range parse_one has signature (sql, read=None, dialect=None, into=None, **opts), and Expression.sql(dialect=None, **opts) forwards opts such as normalize and pretty to the Generator, which accepts both. Dialect None is valid. I did not run it against an installed sqlglot, so this rests on my knowledge of the sqlglot API. Minor note: normalize=True normalizes identifiers rather than keyword casing, and the docstring wording is loose on that, but the kwargs are accepted and the output is canonical.

cli.py:516-527 declares fail_under: float | None = typer.Option(None, '--fail-under', min=0.0, max=100.0). pyproject.toml:48 pins typer>=0.12,<1. In Typer 0.12+ the min/max kwargs map to click.FloatRange for float types, and Optional/union-with-None is unwrapped. With default None and the flag absent, Click does not run conversion, so the value is None. When the flag is given, the value is parsed as float and range-checked against [0,100]. Caveat from my knowledge of Click, not read in this run: a literal 'nan' may slip past the comparison.

The docstring (cli.py:541-543) says an ERROR row shows the same sanitized message an MCP client would get, and that the underlying cause is logged to stderr. That holds only for agent-raised exceptions. query_database.py:240-274 wraps tool-internal failures in RuntimeError(_INTERNAL_ERROR_MESSAGE) and calls logger.exception first. Nothing in src configures logging (no basicConfig/addHandler), so those records reach stderr only through Python's last-resort handler at WARNING and above. Two other ERROR paths in eval/runner.py break the claim. (1) Lines 195-205: when the agent produced no SQL, the row carries a runner-authored message ('agent did not produce a SQL statement...'). It is not an MCP client message and nothing is logged. (2) Lines 213-222: when compare() raises (for example ValueError for an unknown dialect), the row carries f'{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}' and nothing is logged. Also, runner.py:192 prefixes the exception type name ('RuntimeError: ...'), so the row text is not identical to what an MCP client gets. The query_database.py:306-310 path puts the unsanitized agent answer into AgentRunError, and that answer is the text shown. The 'An ERROR row' wording is absolute, and ERROR rows from the no-SQL and compare-failure paths contradict it.
